name: Benefit Cosmetics
desc: San Francisco prestige cosmetics brand founded in 1976, owned by LVMH since 1999, known for brow products, mascara and Benetint.
products: Brow products, mascara, cosmetics, Brow Bar services
customers: Consumers via prestige retailers and Brow Bars
markets: 50+ countries worldwide including the US, UK and Canada, through prestige retail counters and Brow Bars

alt_indicators.evidence: Operates in 50+ countries with 3,200+ points of sale
5,000+ Brow & Beauty Experts globally (LVMH page); Clay lists 4,949 employees
#1 prestige mascara brand in US, UK and Canada (Circana 2023); #1 brow brand worldwide (own claim)
Clay modelled bracket USD 1B-10B (estimate, not reported)

fit_rationale: Consumer beauty brand with 3,200 counters in 50+ countries could run retail promotions; but F1 audience skews male versus its brow-and-mascara core, and LVMH already holds a group F1 deal.
category_conflict: potential: parent LVMH holds a current Formula 1 partnership (LVMH, Louis Vuitton, TAG Heuer, Moët Hennessy on roster); SkinCeuticals and ELEMIS are skincare partners
f1_markets: United States, United Kingdom, Canada and other GP countries among its 50+ markets

access.roles: CEO (Christie Fleischer); Chief Marketing Officer; LVMH Perfumes & Cosmetics group partnerships

outstanding: Reported revenue (LVMH does not break out); whether marketing budget is set at brand or group level given LVMH's F1 deal

name: Bershka
desc: Barcelona-based youth fashion retail chain of the Inditex group, with over 850 stores in 74 countries.
products: Clothing, footwear and accessories for young consumers
customers: Young consumers in stores and online
markets: 74 countries across Europe, Latin America, Middle East and Asia; exited China physical retail in 2022

fin.value_orig: EUR 2,177m (Wikipedia infobox, 2021; older than three years)

distress: Closed TMall and physical stores in China in August 2022
fit_rationale: Youth fashion chain with 850+ stores could run F1-themed capsule collections aimed at F1's younger new fans; no B2B case, and Inditex has historically avoided big sports sponsorship.
category_conflict: potential: fashion partners Tommy Hilfiger, Pepe Jeans, Puma, Castore, BOSS hold team deals
f1_markets: Spain, Mexico, Brazil, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Italy and other European GP countries

access.roles: Bershka brand director; Inditex communications and marketing

outstanding: Current Bershka sales from Inditex annual report (2021 figure is old and the infobox figure needs confirmation); brand-level marketing autonomy

name: Founder Group
desc: Chinese conglomerate founded from Peking University, with IT, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, real estate, finance and commodity trading groups.
products: IT hardware and software, healthcare and pharmaceuticals, real estate, financial services, commodities trading
markets: Mainly China, with listed subsidiaries in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hong Kong

fin.value_orig: CNY 133,273.93m (2018; older than three years and before the 2020 restructuring)

distress: Court-supervised bankruptcy restructuring from 2020 (Wikipedia); current owner after restructuring not stated on the page opened
fit_rationale: Large but restructured Chinese conglomerate with mostly domestic B2B and healthcare businesses; brand value outside China is limited and post-restructuring ownership is unclear.

access.roles: Group president office; brand and public relations department

compliance: 2020 bankruptcy restructuring; verify current ownership (page lists Peking University 70% and management 30% pre-restructuring)
outstanding: Current owner and name after restructuring; current revenue; whether the group entity itself is listed (six subsidiaries are listed)

name: Van Mossel
desc: Dutch automotive dealer group with more than 600 branches in seven European countries, plus body repair and car leasing businesses.
products: New and used car sales for 15 brands, servicing, body repair, leasing (Van Mossel Autolease, J&T Autolease, DirectLease, Westlease)
customers: Private and business car buyers, lease customers
marketing_autonomy_basis: Privately owned BV run by owner Eric Berkhof (Wikipedia NL)
markets: Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Denmark, Germany, France and the United Kingdom

signals.what: Acquired Breeze Motor Group and Ocean Automotive in southern England

fit_rationale: Benelux's largest dealer group, owner-led and expanding into the UK; Dutch and Belgian GP hospitality could serve fleet and lease clients, and dealer brands include F1-linked Audi, Ford and Mercedes.
customer_overlap: Sells Audi, Ford and Mercedes-Benz, which are F1 manufacturers (as dealer, not partner)

access.roles: Owner and general director; marketing director

outstanding: Exact acquisition date of UK dealers (dated late 2025 on page); employee figure conflict (10,645 vs 11,000+); website not opened

name: DANA
desc: Indonesian e-wallet and digital payments app launched in 2018, majority held through an Emtek subsidiary with Sinar Mas group investment.
minority_investors: Bank Sinarmas; Dian Swastatika Sentosa (Sinar Mas group), per Wikipedia

alt_indicators.evidence: 20 million users and 1.5 million transactions per day by end of June 2019 (older figure)

fit_rationale: Mass-market Indonesian e-wallet could use F1 for consumer campaigns, but Indonesia hosts no Grand Prix and the user base is entirely domestic, so geography is weak.
category_conflict: potential: payment partners Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Cash App, Revolut, Nu
f1_markets: none (Indonesia not on calendar; Singapore nearest)
outstanding: Current shareholder structure (Wikipedia contradictory on Emtek vs Sinar Mas); current users, revenue, valuation; Emtek listing status
discovery_source: analyst seed list (subsector brainstorm; not from a page)

name: Gategroup Holding
desc: Swiss airline catering and onboard retail group owned by Temasek and RRJ Capital, serving airlines and railways at 200+ locations.
products: Inflight catering (Gategourmet, Servair), onboard retail (Gateretail), serviceware (DeSter), packaged meals and event catering (Gatesolutions), lounges (Uqonic)
customers: Airlines including Lufthansa (Frankfurt, Munich hubs); rail operators TGV Lyria and Iryo
stores_or_sites: 200+ locations; Gategourmet at 135+ airports in 33 countries
markets: 60+ countries; largest revenue in the US, Germany, France and Switzerland

fin.value_orig: CHF 1'553m revenue 2022 (as listed in input; likely a partial figure)

signals.what: Launched new brands Gatesolutions and Uqonic

fit_rationale: B2B caterer whose airline and rail buyers respond to hospitality; F1 paddock and event catering is a natural showcase for Gatesolutions, and its 60-country footprint matches the calendar.
customer_overlap: Airline customers include Lufthansa; F1 airline partners Qatar Airways, Etihad, Singapore Airlines, Gulf Air not confirmed as customers
f1_markets: United States, Germany-adjacent European GPs, France-linked markets, Switzerland not a host; Spain, UK, Australia, Singapore, UAE, Qatar

access.roles: CEO; Chief Commercial Officer; Head of Brand and Communications

compliance: Asiana Airlines litigation against former Gategroup executives (filed 2022)
outstanding: 2025 results; input CHF 1,553m 2022 figure differs from group revenue (possibly a Swiss-entity figure)

name: Norco Co-op
desc: Farmer-owned dairy co-operative founded in 1895 in Lismore, New South Wales, producing milk, cheese and ice cream brands and rural supplies.
products: Milk, cheese, ice cream (Norco, FM, Mighty Cool, Real Iced Coffee, Tornado Shake), private label, rural products
customers: Australian consumers; retailers Coles, Aldi, Harris Farm (private label); milk exports to China
markets: Australia, with milk exports to China

fin.value_orig: AUD 675.3m revenue (balance date 6/22; IBISWorld Top 500 Private 2022 rank 88; marked ^ = IBISWorld revenue estimate for latest year; older than 3 years)

fit_rationale: Regional NSW dairy co-op with supermarket brands sold only in Australia; could theoretically run Melbourne GP promotions, but scale and marketing budgets are modest. Low fit.
outstanding: Reported revenue for FY2023-25 (IBISWorld FY2022 figure is its own estimate); 2016 figure is old

name: Loterie Nationale / Nationale Loterij
desc: Belgium's national lottery, a public-law limited company in Brussels running Lotto, EuroMillions, scratch cards and Scooore sports betting.
products: Lotto, EuroMillions, Keno, Joker+, VikingLotto, EuroDreams, scratch cards, Scooore sports betting
customers: Belgian adult players through retail outlets and online
marketing_autonomy_basis: Public-law company (société anonyme de droit public since 2002); page does not name the shareholder
fit_rationale: Long-standing sports sponsor (Lotto cycling, Standard de Liège) with a mass Belgian audience; a Belgian Grand Prix tie-in suits it, but a state lottery's remit is domestic and lottery advertising rules apply.
category_conflict: potential: Allwyn (lottery) and several betting brands hold F1 deals

access.roles: CEO; Director of Marketing; Head of Sponsorship

compliance: Regulated gambling operator; Belgian gambling advertising restrictions apply
outstanding: Shareholder (state) confirmation; employees; current sponsorship portfolio

name: Vittoria
desc: Italian bicycle tyre and wheelset maker founded in 1953, owned since 2020 by a Milan private equity fund, producing five million tyres.
products: Road, gravel and mountain bike tyres; wheelsets
customers: Cyclists via bike retailers; bicycle manufacturers
stores_or_sites: Sites in Brembate (Italy), Oklahoma City and Salem (USA), Bangkok (Lion Tyres Thailand), Hong Kong, Taipei and Taichung
markets: Global cycling market with operations in Italy, USA, Thailand, Hong Kong and Taiwan

alt_indicators.evidence: Facilities in Italy, USA, Thailand, Taiwan and Hong Kong
Produces 5 million road and mountain bike tyres (Lion Tyres Thailand factory)

fit_rationale: Premium Italian cycling tyre brand could borrow F1's performance-tyre credibility for consumer marketing, but its budget sits in pro cycling and Pirelli owns the tyre story in F1.
category_conflict: potential: Pirelli (official F1 tyre supplier, also sells bicycle tyres); Specialized (cycling) on roster
outstanding: Revenue; current PE owner confirmation (Wikipedia notability notice); pro-cycling sponsorship spend

name: AL-KO
desc: Bavarian family company founded in 1931, making AL-KO garden equipment and automotive components, part of the Primepulse group since 2017.
products: Lawn mowers and garden tools (AL-KO Gardentech); automotive components
customers: Gardening consumers via retail; automotive industry
parent_ultimate: Primepulse SE (co-founded by Raymond and Stefan Kober with Klaus Weinmann)
stores_or_sites: 30+ locations worldwide; plants in Eisenach, Treuenbrietzen, Stromberg (Germany) and Obdach (Austria)

fin.value_orig: over EUR 500m (2019; older than three years, before 2022 sale of Air Technology to Trane)

fit_rationale: Garden-equipment brand sold through DIY retail in Europe; F1 could support retail promotions, but post-divestment scale is uncertain and Einhell and DeWalt already occupy tools.
category_conflict: potential: Einhell and DeWalt (power tools and garden equipment) hold F1 deals; note AL-KO Vehicle Technology brand belongs to DexKo, a different company
f1_markets: Germany-region European GPs: Austria, Italy, Netherlands, Belgium, Spain

access.roles: Management board (Kober family); Head of Marketing

outstanding: Current revenue after the 2022 Air Technology sale; Primepulse listing status; which entity owns the AL-KO brand today

name: Palladium Group
desc: International development advisory, management and implementation firm formed from seven companies including GRM International, Futures Group and CARANA Corporation.
products: Development programme management, impact investing and impact bonds, advisory
customers: Development agencies such as DFID, USAID and AusAID; governments; foundations
markets: 90 countries (2016 figure) across Africa, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Europe

fin.value_orig: AUD 667.9m revenue (balance date 6/21; IBISWorld Top 500 Private 2022 rank 90; older than 3 years)

fit_rationale: Donor-funded development contractor whose clients are aid agencies and governments; corporate hospitality and consumer awareness add little, so F1 fit is low despite its 90-country footprint.
category_conflict: none found; not related to Palladium Hotel Group (on master)
compliance: Wikipedia article carries an undisclosed-paid-editing notice
outstanding: Ownership; HQ; current revenue (figures from 2016-2021); exposure to 2025 donor-funding cuts not checked

name: Escalent
desc: Market research, analytics and brand consultancy with about 1,600 experts in 13 countries, owner of C Space and Hall & Partners since 2023.
products: Market research, data analytics, customer insight communities (C Space), brand research (Hall & Partners)
customers: Companies in automotive, consumer goods, energy, financial services, health, technology, telecom and travel
stores_or_sites: Offices including Detroit, London, Mumbai and Manila
markets: 13 countries including the US, UK, India and the Philippines

alt_indicators.evidence: About 1,600 researchers, data scientists, moderators, creatives and developers

fit_rationale: Research consultancy with a strong automotive and mobility practice (Detroit roots); hospitality could reach brand and insight buyers, but it is a B2B services firm without consumer pull.
